evidence.note: CONFIRMED: bound_show clips long strings but keeps every gate evidence chunk_findings list entry and every triage finding, so items with 100+ review findings overflow the MCP surface budget. Measured on this repo: ddflow_show B-gap-lanes = 137047 chars (gates 73119 triage 55259), DX-lease-progress-breakable ~65KB. Capping the repeatable lists/triage to a fixed count is the fix.

Followed r-gemini-key-load (export GEMINI_API_KEY from [REDACTED:path] before review) and r-surface-budget (cap the MCP body with exact counts, point to ddflow --json show). Agreed with the existing mcp_bound convention: counts are exact, a cut says so, CLI --json is whole.

Added FINDINGS_SHOWN and _cap_findings to bound_show: every list inside a gate record and each gate triage is capped to 10 entries, counted in truncated.findings_cut, all -> ddflow --json show. Regression test test_show_caps_gate_findings_and_triage_and_counts_what_it_left_out fails before (AttributeError FINDINGS_SHOWN + unbounded) and passes after.

chunk_findings.detail: The regression test does not verify the core promise that the **first** findings are kept. It only checks `len(...) == B.FINDINGS_SHOWN`, the cut count, and total JSON size. An implementation that keeps the **last** `B.FINDINGS_SHOWN` findings (or any arbitrary subset of that size) from `chunk_findings` and `triage["critic"]` would satisfy every assertion in this test while still dropping the first findings, contradicting the stated behavior. The test also uses only one gate, so “each gate’s triage” is asserted for only one gate; a broken implementation that caps triage only for the first gate would still pass.

chunk_findings.detail: The regression test claims the bounded output “keep[s] the first findings”, but it constructs all 150 `chunk_findings` entries as identical `dict(finding)` copies and all 150 triage values as identical too. It then asserts only the surviving container length and the aggregate `findings_cut` count. An implementation that keeps the last `FINDINGS_SHOWN` entries, or any arbitrary sample, still preserves each length and the same `(150 - B.FINDINGS_SHOWN) * 2` count, remains under 20 KB, and includes the `--json show` pointer; for triage it also keeps the same number of keys, though not necessarily the first ones. The test is therefore vacuous for the central “first findings are kept, the rest are omitted” behavior.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_mcp_payload_bound.py:test_show_caps_gate_findings_and_triage_and_counts_what_it_left_out

chunk_findings.detail: The ceiling is never enforced. `_cap_findings` only shortens lists longer than 10 and the top-level triage dict; `bound_show` then returns that tree with no check of `json.dumps` size. Given `{"state":"open","gates":{"critic":{"outcome":"passed","evidence":{f"k{i}": "x"*160 for i in range(200)}}}}`, every string is at `TEXT_SHOWN` so `_clip` leaves them whole, no list exceeds `FINDINGS_SHOWN`, `truncated` is omitted, and the result is still about 32 KB — over the 20 KB r-surface-budget the bug names. The same overflow happens with one kept finding whose body is a dict of ~200 long fields, or with ~30 gates each holding 10 clipped findings. The new test only builds one list of 150 small dicts plus one triage map, so it stays under 20 KB and does not fail on these inputs.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/mcp_bound.py:bound_show

chunk_findings.detail: The added leaf-map cap only applies when every value is a non-dict/non-list scalar. A gate-evidence record that maps each id to a detail object still bypasses the cap. Given `{"state":"open","gates":{"critic":{"outcome":"passed","evidence":{f"k{i}": {"note": "x"*160} for i in range(200)}}}}}`, `_cap_findings` sees `evidence` values as dicts, so `all(not isinstance(v, (dict, list))...)` is false; each inner dict has one scalar value, so no list or leaf-map cap fires, and `dropped` stays 0. There is still no final `json.dumps(out)` size check, so `bound_show` returns a payload of roughly 35–36 KB, still over the 20 KB r-surface-budget. The previous all-scalar probe is fixed, but the ceiling is still not enforced for record-valued evidence maps.
chunk_findings.title: `ddflow/surfaces/mcp_bound.py:_cap_findings`

chunk_findings.detail: The new leaf-map regression test does not assert which leaf-map entries survive. An implementation that kept the last `FINDINGS_SHOWN` entries (`dict(list(value.items())[-FINDINGS_SHOWN:])`) would still make this test pass: the kept length is the same, `findings_cut` is the same, and the serialized size stays below 20 KB. Since the cap is documented as “keep the first `FINDINGS_SHOWN`”, the test would not catch that behavior regressing.
chunk_findings.title: `tests/test_mcp_payload_bound.py:test_show_caps_a_leaf_map_the_string_clip_leaves_under_the_threshold`

chunk_findings.detail: The 20 KB ceiling is still not enforced. The new branch only slices a dict when `len(value) > FINDINGS_SHOWN` and every value is a non-dict, non-list scalar, then `bound_show` still returns that tree with no `json.dumps` size check. Given `{"state":"open","gates":{"critic":{"outcome":"passed","evidence":{f"g{i}": {f"k{j}": "x"*160 for j in range(FINDINGS_SHOWN)} for i in range(40)}}}}`, each inner map has length equal to `FINDINGS_SHOWN` so the `>` test does not fire, the outer evidence map has dict values so it is left whole, every string is the same 160-character payload the new regression treats as under `TEXT_SHOWN`, `truncated` is omitted, and the result is on the order of 64 KB — still over the r-surface-budget the bug requires.
